fanoutqa_013953.t: ExxonMobil :: Operations :: Product Solutions :: Refineries :: chunk_0007
fanoutqa_013953.x:
ExxonMobil :: Operations :: Product Solutions :: Refineries :: chunk_0007
ExxonMobil operates 21 refineries worldwide, and claims that 80% of its refining capacity is integrated with chemical or lube basestocks. ExxonMobil's largest refinery overall is its [Beaumont Refinery](/wiki/ExxonMobil_Beaumont_Refinery "ExxonMobil Beaumont Refinery") and its second largest in the United States is its [Baytown Refinery](/wiki/Baytown_Refinery "Baytown Refinery"), located in [Baytown, Texas](/wiki/Baytown,_Texas "Baytown, Texas"). After ExxonMobile committed thousands of violations of federal law at its Baytown facilities between 2005 and 2013, ExxonMobile was ordered to pay $19.95 million (later reduced to $14.25 million), a decision affirmed in 2024 by the Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals.[[51]](#cite_note-guo-52)

Its second largest refinery overall is its [Jurong Island](/wiki/Jurong_Island "Jurong Island") facility in [Singapore](/wiki/Singapore "Singapore"). ExxonMobil's global average refining capacity was 4.6 million barrels per day, with the United States producing a plurality of the company's refining capacity at about 1.77 million barrels per day. ExxonMobil's corporate website claims it refines almost 5 million barrels per day.[[52]](#cite_note-53)[[53]](#cite_note-54)

ExxonMobil was one of few U.S. refiners to expand capacity by a significant margin following an industry downturn suffered during the [COVID-19 pandemic](/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").[[54]](#cite_note-55) The company completed a 250,000 barrels per day expansion at its [Beaumont, Texas](/wiki/Beaumont,_Texas "Beaumont, Texas"), refinery in early 2023.[[55]](#cite_note-56)

**New Mexico**[[a]](#cite_note-9) is a landlocked state in the [Southwestern](/wiki/Southwestern_United_States "Southwestern United States") region of the United States. It is one of the [Mountain States](/wiki/Mountain_States "Mountain States") of the southern [Rocky Mountains](/wiki/Rocky_Mountains "Rocky Mountains"), sharing the [Four Corners](/wiki/Four_Corners "Four Corners") region with [Utah](/wiki/Utah "Utah"), [Colorado](/wiki/Colorado "Colorado"), and [Arizona](/wiki/Arizona "Arizona"). It also borders the state of [Texas](/wiki/Texas "Texas") to the east and southeast, [Oklahoma](/wiki/Oklahoma "Oklahoma") to the northeast, and shares [an international border](/wiki/Mexico-United_States_border "Mexico-United States border") with the [Mexican states](/wiki/Mexican_states "Mexican states") of [Chihuahua](/wiki/Chihuahua_(state) "Chihuahua (state)") and [Sonora](/wiki/Sonora "Sonora") to the south. New Mexico's largest city is [Albuquerque](/wiki/Albuquerque "Albuquerque"), and its [state capital](/wiki/List_of_capitals_in_the_United_States "List of capitals in the United States") is [Santa Fe](/wiki/Santa_Fe,_New_Mexico "Santa Fe, New Mexico"), the oldest state capital in the U.S.—founded in 1610 as the government seat of [Nuevo México](/wiki/Santa_Fe_de_Nuevo_M%C3%A9xico "Santa Fe de Nuevo México") in [New Spain](/wiki/New_Spain "New Spain")—and the highest in elevation, at 6,998 feet (2,133 m).

New Mexico is the [fifth-largest of the fifty states](/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_area "List of U.S. states and territories by area") by area, but with just over 2.1 million residents, ranks [36th in population](/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population "List of U.S. states and territories by population") and [45th in population density](/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population_density "List of U.S. states and territories by population density").[[8]](#cite_note-10) Its climate and g

He then believed that Lee would win the match in March 2016.[[20]](#cite_note-gibney-20) [Hajin Lee](/wiki/Hajin_Lee "Hajin Lee"), a professional Go player and the [International Go Federation](/wiki/International_Go_Federation "International Go Federation")'s secretary-general, commented that she was "very excited" at the prospect of an AI challenging Lee, and thought the two players had an equal chance of winning.[[20]](#cite_note-gibney-20)

Casino Royale (2006 film) :: Production :: Effects :: part 01 :: chunk_0009
In designing the credit sequence for the film, the graphic designer [Daniel Kleinman](/wiki/Daniel_Kleinman "Daniel Kleinman") was inspired by the cover of the 1953 British first edition of *Casino Royale*, which featured Ian Fleming's original design of a playing card bordered by eight red hearts dripping with blood. Kleinman said, "The hearts not only represent cards but the tribulations of Bond's love story. So I took that as inspiration to use playing card graphics in different ways in the titles", like a club representing a puff of gun smoke, and slashed arteries spurting thousands of tiny hearts.[[72]](#cite_note-73) In creating the shadow images of the sequence, Kleinman digitised the footage of Craig and the film's stuntmen on the [Inferno](/wiki/Inferno_(operating_system) "Inferno (operating system)") visual effects system at [Framestore CFC](/wiki/Framestore_CFC "Framestore CFC") in London; the actors' silhouettes were incorporated into more than 20 digitally animated scenes depicting intricate and innovative card patterns. Kleinman decided not to use the female silhouettes commonly seen throughout the Bond title sequences, considering that the women did not fit with both the film's spirit and the storyline following Bond falling in love.[[73]](#cite_note-74)

For the rest of the film, special effects and miniature effects supervisor [Chris Corbould](/wiki/Chris_Corbould "Chris Corbould") returned to a more realistic style of film making and significantly reduced digital effects. According to Corbould, "CGI is a great tool and can be very useful, but I will fight to the tooth and nail to do something for real. Nile :: Sources :: chunk_0003
[![A map of northeast Africa. The Nile is visible as a meandering blue line, running vertically. The river starts at the bottom in green forested area, and goes upward then ends in a blue sea at the top.](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/28/Nile_River_Sources.svg/250px-Nile_River_Sources.svg.png)](/wiki/File:Nile_River_Sources.svg)

The Nile has six [cataracts](/wiki/Nile_cataracts "Nile cataracts")[[e]](#cite_note-27) and several sources.

The source of the Nile is a tributary of the [Rukarara River](/wiki/Rukarara_River "Rukarara River"), in [Nyungwe National Park](/wiki/Nyungwe_National_Park "Nyungwe National Park"), Rwanda, at [2°19′35″S 29°21′30″E﻿ / ﻿2.32639°S 29.35833°E﻿ / -2.32639; 29.35833](https://geohack.toolforge.org/geohack.php?pagename=Nile&params=2_19_35_S_29_21_30_E_), at an elevation of 2,539 meters (8,330 ft).[[2]](#cite_note-SourceCite-2)[[a]](#cite_note-sourceNote-3)[[f]](#cite_note-sourceRivSequence-28) The source is defined as the starting point of the longest year-round watercourse in the [Nile's drainage basin](/wiki/Nile_Basin "Nile Basin").[[2]](#cite_note-SourceCite-2) From this source, the river runs 7,088 kilometers (4,404 mi) to its mouth at the [Mediterranean Sea](/wiki/Mediterranean_Sea "Mediterranean Sea").[[2]](#cite_note-SourceCite-2)[[b]](#cite_note-longest-7) The distance was measured in 2009 along the centerline of the river using satellite imagery.[[2]](#cite_note-SourceCite-2)

The highest sources of the Nile are on the slopes of the [Rwenzori Mountains](/wiki/Rwenzori_Mountains "Rwenzori Mountains") in [Uganda](/wiki/Uganda "Uganda").[[23]](#cite_note-Rwenz-29) The legendary [Mountains of the Moon](/wiki/Mountains_of_the_Moon_(Africa) "Mountains of the Moon (Africa)"), described by the Greek astronomer [Ptolemy](/wiki/Ptolemy "Ptolemy"), have been associated with Rwenzori.[[23]](#cite_note-Rwenz-29)

Capitol building after 1935 fire

Oregon has had three capitol buildings in Salem. A two-story state house, which had been occupied for only two months, burned to the ground in December 1855. Oregon's second capitol building was completed in 1876 on the site of the original. The [Greek Revival](/wiki/Greek_Revival_architecture "Greek Revival architecture")-style building was based in part on the [U.S. Capitol building](/wiki/U.S._Capitol_building "U.S. Capitol building"). The building received its distinctive copper dome in 1893. On April 25, 1935, this building was also destroyed by fire. The third and current [Oregon State Capitol](/wiki/Oregon_State_Capitol "Oregon State Capitol") was completed on the same site in 1938. It faces north instead of west like its predecessor, and is recognizable by its distinctive pioneer statue atop the capitol dome that is plated with gold-leaf and officially named the *[Oregon Pioneer](/wiki/Oregon_Pioneer "Oregon Pioneer")*.

On October 5, 2011, Steve Jobs died, marking the end of an era for Apple.[[136]](#cite_note-136) The next major product announcement by Apple was on January 19, 2012, when Apple's [Phil Schiller](/wiki/Phil_Schiller "Phil Schiller") introduced [iBooks](/wiki/Apple_Books "Apple Books") Textbooks for iOS and iBooks Author for Mac OS X in New York City.[[137]](#cite_note-137) Jobs stated in the biography *Steve Jobs* that he wanted to reinvent the [textbook](/wiki/Textbook "Textbook") industry and education.[[138]](#cite_note-138)

From 2011 to 2012, Apple released the [iPhone 4s](/wiki/IPhone_4s "IPhone 4s")[[139]](#cite_note-139) and [iPhone 5](/wiki/IPhone_5 "IPhone 5"),[[140]](#cite_note-140) which featured improved cameras, an [intelligent software assistant](/wiki/Intelligent_software_assistant "Intelligent software assistant") named [Siri](/wiki/Siri "Siri"), and cloud-synced data with iCloud; the [third-](/wiki/IPad_(third_generation) "IPad (third generation)") and [fourth-generation iPads](/wiki/IPad_(fourth_generation) "IPad (fourth generation)"), which featured [Retina displays](/wiki/Retina_displays "Retina displays");[[141]](#cite_note-141)[[142]](#cite_note-Lightning_strikes_again-142) and the [iPad Mini](/wiki/IPad_Mini "IPad Mini"), which featured a 7.9-inch screen in contrast to the iPad's 9.7-inch screen.[[143]](#cite_note-mini-143) These launches were successful, with the iPhone 5 (released September 21, 2012) becoming Apple's biggest iPhone launch with over two million pre-orders[[144]](#cite_note-144) and sales of three million iPads in three days following the launch of the iPad Mini and fourth-generation iPad (released November 3, 2012).[[145]](#cite_note-145) Apple also released a third-generation 13-inch [MacBook Pro](/wiki/MacBook_Pro "MacBook Pro") with a Retina display and new [iMac](/wiki/IMac "IMac") and [Mac Mini](/wiki/Mac_Mini "Mac Mini") computers.[

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/be/Top_of_Atmosphere.jpg/250px-Top_of_Atmosphere.jpg)](/wiki/File:Top_of_Atmosphere.jpg)

Earth's atmosphere

All of the Solar System planets [except Mercury](/wiki/Atmosphere_of_Mercury "Atmosphere of Mercury")[[118]](#cite_note-119) have substantial [atmospheres](/wiki/Atmosphere "Atmosphere") because their gravity is strong enough to keep gases close to the surface. Saturn's largest moon [Titan](/wiki/Titan_(moon) "Titan (moon)") also has a substantial atmosphere thicker than that of Earth;[[119]](#cite_note-120) Neptune's largest moon [Triton](/wiki/Triton_(moon) "Triton (moon)")[[120]](#cite_note-Solar_System-121) and the dwarf planet [Pluto](/wiki/Pluto "Pluto") have more tenuous atmospheres.[[121]](#cite_note-Lellouch_2015-122) The larger giant planets are massive enough to keep large amounts of the light gases hydrogen and helium, whereas the smaller planets lose these gases into [space](/wiki/Interplanetary_medium "Interplanetary medium").[[122]](#cite_note-123) Analysis of exoplanets suggests that the threshold for being able to hold on to these light gases occurs at about 2.0+0.7  
−0.6 *M*🜨, so that Earth and Venus are near the maximum size for rocky planets.[[54]](#cite_note-ChenKipping-55)
